messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Sev2 — Helix Health (enterprise: helix-health) EU dedicated routing degraded. Trigger: high 5xx rate from routing-layer in eu-west-1. Pager: ops-pager. Runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-routing-degrade. Thread created 1729004321.

maya (oncall): seeing ~20% 5xx on dedicated pool eu-west-1 for Helix. Latency is normal for other customers, routing table seems to be dropping some backends. Paging now.

rami (sre): ack. grabbing logs and routing table. can you post affected customer contacts (CS/AE) so we can draft a targeted external notice?

jess (customer-success): Alex M (helix main contact), alex.m@helixhealth.com, +44 7700 900111; backup is Priya K (priya.k@helixhealth.com). They're on-call for their infra. High-touch SLA on Dedicated (SLA-24).

maya (oncall): thanks. quick mitigation plan: 1) isolate Helix traffic to a fallback routing group, 2) restart routing proxy on node eu-west-1-03, 3) if restart fails, failover to eu-west-2 dedicated capacity.

olivia (eng-runtime): re: 1) we have a safe fallback variant in the routing config (fallback-group-v2) that drops non-essential metadata and keeps sessions. Prep command ready.

rami (sre): running log gather: 
```
curl -s "https://logs.internal/api/query?service=routing&env=prod&customer=helix-health&since=10m" | jq .summary
```
Prelim shows increased `backend_unavailable` events on node eu-west-1-03.

ops-pager: paging maya, rami, olivia. Please respond.

maya (oncall): I'm SSHing to eu-west-1-03 now. pulling `journalctl -u redwood-routing`

rami (sre): while maya connects, drafting the external customer status note. Here's a short tailored impact statement for Helix to review: 

"Helix Health — Incident (eu-west-1 dedicated routing) — We are experiencing intermittent request failures for Helix Health customers served from the EU dedicated pool. Some requests return 5xx. We are actively investigating and have isolated the impacted routing node. We will perform a controlled restart and, if necessary, fail traffic to a nearby dedicated capacity to restore service. Estimated initial mitigation window: 10-30 minutes. We will update within 15 minutes or on additional findings."

jess (customer-success): good. please also add the mitigation steps for them so they know we won't purging KV caches etc. Add: we will not restart customer VMs or touch customer data.

rami (sre): updated draft with that note. prepping a statuspage entry (internal draft): 

Statuspage draft:
```
Component: Dedicated Routing EU (eu-west-1) — partial outage for Helix Health.
Impact: Intermittent 5xx errors leading to failed API calls for Helix Health traffic from EU dedicated pool.
What we're doing: Isolating impacted routing node, controlled restart of routing proxy, and preparing cross-region failover if needed.
Customer impact: Helix Health may see increased error rates for short lived windows; no data loss expected.
ETA: initial mitigation in 10-30 minutes; updates every 15 minutes.
```

maya (oncall): restart attempt on eu-west-1-03 coming up: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-routing` — I'll tail logs after.

olivia (eng-runtime): hold on on failover until restart completes. fallback routing can cause a short session reset; we should prefer restart first.

maya (oncall): restart returned exit 0. tail shows repeated TLS handshake errors to backend service A (ip 10.3.7.12). suspect ephemeral backend overload or momentary network blip.

rami (sre): switching to fallback-group-v2 for Helix while backend stabilizes. Command: 
```
/redwoodctl routing update --customer helix-health --set-group fallback-group-v2 --region eu-west-1 --reason "fallback to mitigage routing-node instability"
```
Executing now.

ops-pager: automation run shows `200 OK` for the routing update. Monitoring for error rate drop.

maya (oncall): error rate dropped to ~3% 5xx (from 20%) within 90s. Latency stable. Good.

jess (customer-success): drafting customer notification to send to Alex & Priya. Proposed message below — please edit for legal/ops: 

"Hi Alex / Priya — We detected intermittent request failures (5xx) for Helix Health requests via the EU dedicated pool beginning at 12:24 UTC. Our team isolated the affected routing node and applied a temporary routing fallback to restore traffic. The service is now significantly recovered, error rate reduced to baseline but we are continuing monitoring and will perform a post-incident analysis. No customer data was modified. We will send a follow-up with RCA and next steps. — Redwood Inference ops"

rami (sre): good. add estimated timeline for RCA (72 hours typical for enterprise).

jess (customer-success): added. I'll send now and CC AE and account exec.

maya (oncall): handing off active incident to night oncall (rami takes over). Handoff summary: 
- Incident: Helix Health dedicated routing degraded (eu-west-1)
- Time started: 1729004321 (~12:24 UTC)
- Actions taken: restarted routing proxy on eu-west-1-03; applied fallback routing group fallback-group-v2 for Helix; monitored error rate drop from ~20% to ~3%.
- Next steps: monitor for recurrence, schedule RCA, consider replacing eu-west-1-03 node if TLS errors continue.

rami (sre): taking it. I'll own the follow-up and coordinate RCA. Quick ops note for runbook: we should add a step to check the TLS cert reload cron and kernel level sndbuf metrics for that node.

olivia (eng-runtime): filing a ticket with infra to inspect eu-west-1-03 NIC and kernel ring buffers. tagging infra on the ticket.

ops-pager: reminder: if error rate creeps above 5% for >5 minutes, escalate to Sev1 and notify leadership.

jess (customer-success): Helix contacts notified (email sent at 12:38 UTC). They replied: "Thanks for the quick mitigation — please keep us posted on RCA."

rami (sre): finalizing statuspage public update and internal incident record. Public update (short): 
"Update: We mitigated intermittent request failures for Helix Health on the EU dedicated routing pool. Traffic was routed to a fallback group while we stabilize the impacted node. Error rates have reduced; monitoring continues."

maya (oncall): marking as mitigated in incident tracker (mitigated=true) and adding notes for follow-up: node replacement candidate, add TLS cert reload alert.

rami (sre): thanks all. closing the paging rotation. Will post RCA draft in #postmortems within 72h.

jess (customer-success): leaving a post-incident customer note template in their engagement file: "We applied a temporary routing fallback and will provide an RCA within 72 hours. No data loss. If you need a dedicated post-mortem call, let us know times."

olivia (eng-runtime): also adding a unit test in the routing integration tests to exercise backend TLS reload case.

incident-bot: Incident thread updated: status=mitigated, severity=2, owners=[rami (sre)]. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/1729004321

maya (oncall): thanks team. signing off.

rami (sre): signing off on-shift; I'll take ownership of RCA and keep comms with jess for Helix.

(End of thread)
